solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Discouraging sounds, we hear, getting drink

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word in question is only being said out loud, and the spelling changes

parts.note: boos are the jeers a crowd makes to discourage a performer

explanation.surface: Someone is put off by jeering and turns to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Booze is the informal word for alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Locals taken with Scot, not a civilised sort

parts.note: a local is a pub or bar, and the plural gives two bars
Ian is a typically Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: Pubs and a Scotsman create an uncivilised character.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage 'the local' is a person's nearby pub; two of them give BAR BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbarian is a person regarded as uncultured or uncivilised.

clue.text: Tender Mercian King reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly says we only hear the word said, not see it written

parts.note: Offa was an 8th-century king of Mercia, of Offa's Dyke fame

explanation.surface: A gentle Anglo-Saxon king, so the story goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To tender is to formally offer, as in tendering a bid.

clue.text: Titled figure with support losing power previously

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman with a title

indicators.note: losing power means the letter P, the physics symbol for power, is removed

parts.note: a pier is a pillar supporting a bridge

explanation.surface: A noble once supported, now stripped of influence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing power' removes P from PIER, leaving IER.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier means at a previous time, before now.

clue.text: Syrup from Caribbean island largely in East

indicators.note: largely means most of the island's name is used, its final letter dropped

parts.note: Grenada is an island nation in the Caribbean
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sweet syrup sourced from a Caribbean island, mostly sold in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenadine is a red pomegranate-flavoured syrup used in cocktails.

clue.text: One affected by moving air with good German songs, not English

indicators.note: not English means one E, the abbreviation for English, is dropped

parts.note: Lieder are German art songs

explanation.surface: A good set of German songs moves along on the breeze, minus the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not English' removes one E from LIEDER, giving LIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A glider is an engineless aircraft carried by air currents.

clue.text: A poet I fancy receiving greeting in country

indicators.note: receiving says the rearranged letters take in the greeting
fancy says the letters of the preceding words are arranged decoratively anew

parts.note: hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A poet dreams of a warm welcome in a foreign land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges A POET I into ETOPIA, and 'receiving' puts HI inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethiopia is a country in the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: Made aware Welshman is entertaining Irish broadcaster

indicators.note: is entertaining means the Welshman's name hosts the broadcaster inside it

parts.note: Aled is a Welsh man's name
RTE is the Irish national broadcaster

explanation.surface: A Welshman learns something while hosting a visitor from Irish TV.
explanation.definitionFit: Alerted means warned, made aware of something.

clue.text: Complete wrench maybe

definitions.meaning: to carry out or fulfil a plan, the verb sense
a wrench is an example of a tool, the noun sense

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means put into effect; as a noun, a tool such as a wrench.

clue.text: Record time held by upcoming Frenchman

indicators.note: held by says the time letter sits inside the Frenchman
upcoming in a down clue means the name reads upward, so backwards

parts.note: Rene is a French man's name

explanation.surface: A Frenchman on his way up keeps a timed record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upcoming' turns RENE into ENER and 'held by' puts T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter data is to record it in a ledger or system.

clue.text: Brief rush to get changed and brighten up

indicators.note: to get changed says the letters of the two preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A quick dash to change clothes and smarten oneself up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief rush' looks like the definition of a short dash, but those nine letters are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To refurbish a place is to renovate and brighten it up.

clue.text: Father taken in by message axeing principal person abroad

indicators.note: taken in by says the father's word goes inside the trimmed message
axeing principal means the message word loses its first letter

parts.note: a text is a message sent by phone
Pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A dad receives a text that cuts out the most important person while away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'message' wants to be the definition alongside 'person abroad'; it supplies TEXT, whose principal (first) letter is axed.
explanation.definitionFit: An expatriate is someone living outside their native country.

clue.text: Excellent merit possibly in TV coverage?

parts.note: A1 means first-class or excellent, written AI with the figure as a letter I

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of the following word may be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Would excellent merit win a broadcaster's attention on television?
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (excellent) becomes AI when the digit 1 is read as letter I; 'possibly' rearranges MERIT into RTIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Airtime is the broadcasting time given to a subject on radio or television.

clue.text: Last longer than striking flower

parts.note: workers who are striking are out
a flower here is something that flows, a river: the Wear in northeast England

explanation.surface: A dramatic bloom that outlives the others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is the crossword trick of a river (a thing that flows); the Wear runs through Durham.
explanation.definitionFit: To outwear something is to outlast it, staying in use longer.

clue.text: Hurt among group of twelve?

parts.note: among means in
a jury traditionally has twelve members

explanation.surface: Someone is hurt among a group of twelve people.
explanation.definitionFit: An injury is harm done to the body, a hurt.

clue.text: Petty official from Japan improvised short bow

parts.note: J is the international vehicle code for Japan

indicators.note: improvised says the letters of the following words are put together in a new way

explanation.surface: A pedantic official from Japan makes a quick bow on the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' looks like an instruction to trim 'bow', but it is part of the fodder. A JOBSWORTH is British slang for a rule-bound petty official.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a minor functionary who enforces rules rigidly.

clue.text: Family about to forward first bit of sizable generosity

parts.note: kin means family or relatives

indicators.note: about says the following word is turned round

parts.note: to send on is to forward

indicators.note: first bit of means only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A family about to pass on the first part of a sizeable generous gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the synonym of 'to forward' backwards; 'about to' reads as 'ready to' in the surface but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindness is the quality of being generous and considerate.

clue.text: Not looking ahead too much, what schoolchildren like?

definitions.meaning: focused only on the near future
pupils prefer a brief school term

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means concerned with the near future, and punningly a brief school session.

clue.text: By the sound of it, important sporting group in part of harbour

indicators.note: By the sound of it says the word is only heard, not written

parts.note: a key side is an important team

explanation.surface: An important team seems to be found somewhere on the docks.
explanation.walkthrough: KEY SIDE (important team) sounds like QUAYSIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A quayside is the area beside a quay where ships dock.

clue.text: Crash of lone bus involving middle of bus? It's unclear

indicators.note: involving says the scrambled letters wrap around the extra piece
crash of says the letters of the next words are smashed into a new order
middle of means the central letter of the second bus is taken

explanation.surface: A lone bus crashes in the middle of its route, and the cause is unclear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crash of' turns LONE BUS into NEBLOUS; 'involving' puts U, the middle of the second 'bus', inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebulous means vague or hazy, so unclear.

clue.text: Upcoming regulation almost caught woman's dog

indicators.note: Upcoming in a down clue means the trimmed word reads upward, so in reverse
almost means the final letter is lost

parts.note: a rule is a regulation
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
her is the possessive for a woman

explanation.surface: A new rule nearly catches a woman's dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims RULE to RUL, and 'Upcoming' turns it to LUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A lurcher is a British crossbreed of greyhound type.

clue.text: Greek and German found in cave

parts.note: Otto is a typical German man's name

explanation.surface: A Greek and a German are discovered in a cave.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotto is a small picturesque cave.

clue.text: Answer I start to provoke inside versatile store

indicators.note: inside says the I and the first letter go within the rearranged store
versatile, able to change readily, says the letters of store are rearranged
start to means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: I begin to provoke a reply in a flexible shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'versatile' rearranges STORE into ROSTE, and IP goes inside after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick, sharp reply, an answer.

clue.text: Change the direction of seedy place above empty resort

parts.note: a dive is a disreputable bar or club

indicators.note: empty means only the outer letters of the word remain, the middle removed

explanation.surface: Reroute a sleazy club above a deserted holiday town.
explanation.definitionFit: To divert something is to turn it from its course.

clue.text: Noted cricketer excited crowd with extremes of energy

indicators.note: excited says the letters of crowd are stirred up into a new order
extremes of means the first and last letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A famous cricketer gets the crowd excited with his energy.
explanation.walkthrough: Colin COWDREY was a famous England batsman of the 1950s and 60s.
explanation.definitionFit: Colin Cowdrey was a celebrated England Test cricketer and captain.

clue.text: Cold rounds brought up as sign of short break?

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means the word reads upward, reversed

parts.note: ammo means ammunition, rounds

explanation.surface: Cold, then rounds of ammunition carried upward during a brief pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns AMMO into OMMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A comma is a punctuation mark indicating a brief pause.

clue.text: Confession of spy? Something put in one's mouth

parts.note: a confession begins I am, shortened to I'm
a plant is a spy placed inside an organisation

explanation.surface: A spy owns up; then something is stuck in his mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm a plant' would be a spy's confession; the definition refers to a dental implant.
explanation.definitionFit: A dental implant is an artificial tooth root fitted into the jaw.

clue.text: Woman staying among champagne socialists

indicators.note: staying among says the name is lodged inside the following words

explanation.surface: A lady stays among left-wingers who love luxury.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'champagne socialist' is British for a wealthy left-winger who enjoys luxury.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Agnes is one female given name, so it stands for a woman.

clue.text: Delight recalling well-kept hotel

indicators.note: recalling, calling back, says the preceding word is read in reverse

parts.note: trim means neat and well-kept
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Pleasure in remembering a beautifully maintained hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalling' reads as remembering in the surface, but it signals calling the word back, reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Mirth is amusement or delight shown in laughter.

clue.text: Basically popular perfume

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
an essence is a concentrated scent or perfume

explanation.surface: A perfume that is fundamentally a crowd-pleaser.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means fundamentally, at its core.

clue.text: Loathsome born hater getting agitated

indicators.note: getting agitated says the letters of the preceding words are stirred about

explanation.surface: A person who hates from birth, growing worked up, is repellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Abhorrent means detestable, inspiring loathing.

clue.text: Not all keep sombre in course

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Stay gloomy, though not entirely, out at the racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave 'in course' as definition; 'in' is a link word, as 'Epsom' substitutes for 'course' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs is an English racecourse, home of the Derby.
